unit: Unit 12: Everyday Life with Your Computer
title: Reading and Saving PDFs
drDigitalIntro:
PDFs are one of the most common things you will download. A PDF looks the same on every device, which makes it perfect for forms, receipts, and instruction manuals.

To open one from the internet:
1. Click a PDF link — the browser usually opens it right away in its built-in viewer.
2. Use the + and - buttons at the top to enlarge small print.
3. Scroll through the pages like a web page.

To save one:
1. Click the download arrow in the viewer's toolbar.
2. The file lands in your Downloads folder.
3. To read it later, open your file manager — Finder on a Mac, File Explorer on Windows — go to Downloads, and double-click it.

To turn anything printable into a PDF:
1. Press Ctrl+P (Command+P on a Mac) to open the Print window.
2. Under Printer, choose 'Save as PDF'.
3. Click Save and pick where to put it.

Tip: PDFs from your bank or doctor matter — save them in a named folder so you can find them again.

playgroundTask.goal: You found, saved, and showed me a real PDF

steps.say: Find a PDF on the internet and open it.
steps.detail: An easy way: search for any recipe or user manual followed by the letters PDF. Click a result that opens right in the browser — you will see pages, like paper on the screen.
Look for the download arrow in the viewer's toolbar (usually top-right). Click it — the file lands in your Downloads folder.

steps.say: Show me the PDF you just saved.
steps.detail: Click the button and pick the file from your Downloads folder. I check two things: it is really a PDF, and it was saved in the last hour — so it has to be the one you just downloaded. I never upload it anywhere.

drDigitalSuccess: That is the whole journey — find, save, and find it again on your own computer. Forms, receipts, and manuals all travel as PDFs, and now they are all yours to keep.
drDigitalHint: Stuck finding one? Search for 'apple pie recipe pdf'. The download arrow is in the PDF viewer's own toolbar, not the browser's menu.
